A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Stable Deep Reinforcement Learning via Isotropic Gaussian Representations. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including the new Appendices F–H in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 label-shuffling experiments, Atari evaluations with PQN and PPO, Isaac Gym results, and representation ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds synthetic tracking experiments, alternative-regularizer comparisons, and spectral measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions apply the same SIGReg characteristic-function matching objective to randomly projected embeddings. The proposed regularizer, its integration into RL training, and its components remain unchanged; the additional regularizers are comparison methods.

E1.justification: The CIFAR-10, Atari, and Isaac Gym coverage is retained. Appendix F adds a distinct synthetic non-stationary linear-regression task with Gaussian and Laplace inputs, periodic target switches, and deliberately directed target drift.

E2.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix G add evaluated embedding norm regularization, simplicial embeddings, and weight orthogonalization comparators on Atari-10 with PQN. Covariance whitening/VICReg, alternative target distributions, Kron, and multi-skip comparisons were already present in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces controlled target-switching and directed-drift protocols, conditioning sweeps, and feature dimensions 2, 8, and 32. Appendix H adds eigenvalue-entropy and baseline-to-SIGReg condition-number measurements. The original benchmark settings and hyperparameter Tables 4–9 are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing distribution and loss-component ablations, v3 adds controlled tests of conditioning, tail behavior, dimensionality, and drift strength in Appendix F. Appendix H adds spectral analyses covering both successful and unsuccessful environments, directly examining whether improved representation geometry accompanies improved returns.

E5.justification: The existing five-seed averaging and shaded variability reporting remain. Appendix F additionally reports individual trajectories across three random seeds, including Figures 18–29 and 31. This adds seed-level reporting without establishing additional runs for the original benchmarks.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–3 retain their values. New Table 10 reports average improvements of -1% for embedding norm regularization, 17% for simplicial embeddings, and 219% for weight orthogonalization, alongside the retained 305% SIGReg result. Figures 18–32 and Tables 11–12 add tracking and spectral results.

T1.justification: The tracking theorem, fixed-covariance assumptions, isotropy argument, and Stein-residual derivation through Equation 58 are retained. V3 makes the expectation measures explicit and expands the Gaussianity explanation, but these clarify the existing mathematics without adding or correcting a substantive theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims that isotropic Gaussian representations favor stable tracking and that SIGReg improves representation quality and RL performance. The new experiments supply supporting evidence without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V3 proposes additional explanations for differing PQN/PPO gains and analyzes failures involving sparse rewards or limited representational demands in Appendix C.4.2. Appendix H explicitly recognizes that higher spectral entropy can accompany worse performance. These additions substantially qualify the interpretation and applicability of the retained results.

D1.justification: Appendix F documents synthetic sampling, target selection, covariance scaling, and drift construction, including the equal-variance construction in Figure 30. Existing hyperparameter tables and the code-access link are unchanged. Toy SGD settings and tuning details for the new comparators remain incompletely specified.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds positioning relative to Kalman–Bucy stability analysis and stochastic approximation. V3 also adds references supporting the new regularizer comparisons and XQC, while removing references accompanying the deleted multi-task future-work suggestion. The established representation-learning positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. V3 adds Sections 3.5 and 4.5, Appendices F–H, acknowledgments, and an impact statement, alongside localized explanatory edits and the expanded first-author name. The original narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V3 retains Figures 1–17 and Tables 1–9, with placement and caption-format changes, and adds Figures 18–32 and Tables 10–12. The new tracking trajectories, error curves, comparator table, and spectral tables substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the additional regularizer comparisons, tracking tests, and spectral diagnostics provide useful corroboration, while the failure-case discussion better qualifies applicability. The gains are limited by incomplete experimental details and caption/plot inconsistencies, such as Figure 31's task-switch times. The original main results and formal guarantees remain unchanged.
